properties.Name: Kom El-Ahmar Qabli (Mahmoudiah)
properties.Location: lies about 15 kilometres north of Damanhur
properties.Data: The actual site of Kom el-Ahmar is a large, oval area of about 650 metres from east to west by 450 metres from north to south.
properties.Importance: one of the best known sites in Beheira archaeology, as the bath-house was investigated and a stone head of a Ptolemaic queen, another statue head, and, thirteen further statue heads were found here

properties.Name: Kom El-Ahmar Bahari (Sidi Salem)
properties.Location: lies to the east of Tell Foqaa
properties.Data: Is a low mound, perhaps as much as 10 metres above the level of the surrounding fish farms. It is approximately 250 metres from north to south and 360 metres from east to west and so is quite substantial in size.
properties.Importance: Forms an interesting cluster of settlements, along with those on the edge of the former marshland, now agricultural land in the north.

properties.Name: Burj El-Burullus
properties.Location: It is located near Al-Fanar Beach in the Baltim resort town, overlooking the Mediterranean coast.
properties.Data: It was constructed in 1869, during the reign of Khedive Ismail, at a height of approximately 60 meters.
properties.Importance: In the past, it was used to guide ships arriving from the Mediterranean, utilizing a kerosene-powered lamp with a range of up to 17 nautical miles. It stands as the only surviving lighthouse from that era.

properties.Name: Moseque El-Bakie
properties.Location: It is located in the city of Fuwwah, in the Kafr El-Sheikh Governorate.
properties.Data: It was built in the late 18th or early 19th century AD.
properties.Importance: It is one of the historic elevated mosques in the city of Fuwwah, Kafr El-Sheikh Governorate.

properties.Name: Moseque Sidi Yousef El-Sotohi
properties.Location: It is located in the village of Al-Banna’in (also known as Al-Yawasifa or Al-Wasaifa) within the Burullus Center of Kafr El-Sheikh Governorate.
properties.Data: Established in 1924, the mosque received royal attention during the reign of King Farouk, who ordered its restoration and the preservation of its original architectural style. It houses the shrine of Sayyid Yusuf Al-Rishi Al-Rifa'i Al-Hasani.
properties.Importance: It is considered one of the oldest and most renowned mosques in Burullus; it is said to be the first mosque in Egypt's history to be placed under the administration of the Ministry of Endowments (Awqaf).

properties.Name: Kom Mazen
properties.Location: It lies approximately 3.5 kilometres north of a larger town called Bulin
properties.Age: Late Ptolemaic and Early Roman periods
properties.Data: This area is now covered by an orchard and fields. Some pottery is visible lying on the fields and in drainage ditches, but it is only a light scatter of material.
properties.Importance: There is a strong suggestion that if there were a true kom in the area, it has been completely removed. The pottery from the augers in Kom Mazen must relate to the relatively recent occupation of the area, perhaps over the last one thousand years

properties.Name: Kom Adda
properties.Location: lies some 8 kilometres north-west of Abu Matamir, a little further along the same road as Abu Guduur. The site may be the same as Kom Abdul Ghadi
properties.Data: The site is apparently built over by a village. The extent of the village is approximately 220 metres from north-west to south-east and up to 300 metres from south-west to north-east.
properties.Importance: the site is the curious water feature to the south-west. There is a crescent-shaped, enclosed lake next to the village which may be a relic of an ancient river distributary or ox-bow lake.

properties.Name: Kom El-Mahar
properties.Location: isolated in farmland, to the east of the Nubariyah Canal and approximately 3 kilometres south-west of Sidi Ghazi village.
properties.Data: The site covers an area of approximately 440 metres from east to west and 240 metres from north to south at its greatest extent. The main part of the site consists of a 10-12 metre high mound on the north of the area covered in pottery, the latter inclu
properties.Importance: The pottery from the site is of Late Ptolemaic to Late Roman in date, suggesting that the site may have been a Ptolemaic foundation continuing as a town into the Roman period

properties.Name: Kom El-Farag
properties.Location: a modern town, approximately 13 kilometres north-west of Abu Matamir.
properties.Data:
The cemetery part of Kom Farag lies to the
north-west and may be a remnant of one of the older mounds in the area, such as Kom el
51 Hanache/Hanash. The small mound is around a maximum of 1.5 metres above ground level
and covered in graves.
properties.Importance:
It lies on both the Tirat Abdel al-Fatah and Tirat al
Hajar, main drainage channels and possibly close to the channel of one of the earlier Canopic
distributaries on the western side of Beheira.

properties.Name: Kom El-Gel
properties.Location:
The site at Ezbet Abd el-Qadir at-Tawil and lies approximately 17
kilometres north-west of Abu Matamir
properties.Data:
a flat top and gently sloping northern side, perhaps rising up to 3 or 4 metres above the level of the roads and fields around it. The extent of the mound is
270 metres from north to south and 220 metres from east to west.

properties.Name: Kom Ishu
properties.Location:
The site is situated upon a limestone outcrop at the edge of the northern limestone
formation, approximately 12 kilometres west-south-west of Kafr ed-Dawar
properties.Data:
The dimensions of the rocky
outcrop are 150 metres from east to west and 200 metres from north to south, with the
outlying foothills and village

properties.Name: Kom El-Qadi
properties.Location: The site lies to the south of the main Cairo to Alexandria road, approximately 6 kilometres south of Kafr ed-Dawar
properties.Data: Covering an area of about 370 metres from east to west and 250 metres from north west to south-east
properties.Importance: In the village to the west there is a Roman bath-house which has been restored recently and includes part of the concrete floor of a tholos,  possible underfloor furnaces and some rectangular tanks.

properties.Name: Tabiya El-Abd
properties.Location: It extends from the Burj Rashid area in the east to the village of Al-Maadiya (Abu Qir/Idku) in the west.
properties.Data: Its walls were constructed of thick limestone or brick and featured stone vaults and passageways designed to withstand naval bombardment, in addition to high, crenellated ramparts for surveillance.
properties.Importance: It was built to protect the town and the coast from the west, and for surveillance and defense.

properties.Name: Port Thonis, Heracleion
properties.Location: Was a major ancient Egyptian port city and religious center located about 32 kilometers (20 miles) northeast of Alexandria in Abu Qir Bay, resting underwater today
properties.Data: Also known by its Egyptian name Thonis and Greek name Heracleion. Founded around the 8th century BC, it served as Egypt's mandatory gateway and customs port for maritime trade from Greece and the Mediterranean before Alexandria was founded.
properties.Importance: Sunk into the sea due to earthquakes, tsunamis, and soil liquefaction. The findings: Colossal red granite statues (including a 5.4-meter statue of the god Hapy), 64 shipwrecks, 700 ancient anchors, gold plaques, and the grand temple of Amun.

properties.Name: Antique Tahona
properties.Location: It is located on Dahliz al-Malik Street (also known as Al-Amsili Street) and is attached to the famous historic Al-Amsili House.
properties.Data: Dating back to the 18th century (the Ottoman era), it was established by Uthman Agha al-Tubji (the artillery commander in Rosetta). It was named "Abu Shahin" after the last miller to operate it before it ceased operations.
properties.Importance: It served a charitable purpose, having been established as a *waqf* (endowment) with proceeds dedicated to the maintenance and staffing of the Al-Mahalli Mosque—the largest mosque in Rosetta at the time.

properties.Name: Museum Rosetta
properties.Location: Is located on the west bank at the mouth of the Nile River where it meets the Mediterranean Sea, 65 km northeast of Alexandria.
properties.Data: The house of Hussein Arab Kuli—who served as the Governor of Rosetta from 1844 to 1849—was selected to serve as a military museum. The structure comprises a ground floor and three additional stories, all designed in the Islamic architectural style.
properties.Importance: It was built to commemorate the victory of the city's residents over the Fraser Expedition on September 19, 1807.

properties.Name: Citadle Qitbai
properties.Location: On the western bank of the Rosetta Branch of the Nile River, approximately 6 kilometers north of the city of Rosetta in Beheira Governorate
properties.Data: It was built by the Mamluk Sultan Al-Ashraf Qaitbay in 886 AH (1482 CE) to repel Crusader raids and protect the Mamluk state's coasts and the port of Rosetta from pirate attacks.
properties.Importance: To prevent commercial ships from entering the Nile River from the Mediterranean. In August 1799, the citadel witnessed the discovery of the famous Rosetta Stone by the French officer Bouchard during restoration work carried out during the French campaign.
